summary: Build practical coastal and marine data management skills with ISO, OGC, QGIS, and PostGIS workflows. Review the five-day course.
lede: Coastal and marine data management brings bathymetry, habitat, shoreline, and survey information into traceable, quality-checked workflows. Designed for intermediate marine geoscientists, GIS analysts, hydrographic surveyors, and ocean data managers, the course covers creating metadata records, assessing spatial and attribute quality, and designing marine geodatabases. Participants also practise integrating raster and vector data and preparing quality-controlled maps and dashboard specifications.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who manage, analyse, validate, publish, or govern coastal and marine geoscience data. It is designed for intermediate practitioners who already work with spatial, environmental, hydrographic, oceanographic, or geological datasets and need a more consistent data-management workflow.
modules: Raster, Sensor, and Ocean Data Integration
prerequisites: You should have practical experience with spatial, environmental, hydrographic, oceanographic, or geological datasets. Familiarity with GIS concepts, coordinate reference systems, and spreadsheet-based data review is expected. No programming is required for completion, although basic exposure to SQL or Python can support optional workflow exploration. Bring a laptop if your delivery arrangement permits hands-on access to QGIS and PostgreSQL/PostGIS.
